reason: The hypothesis makes specific mechanistic claims about interface structure, dislocation behavior, and creep in FCC/BCC HEA multilayers, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the unique behavior of such complex interfaces, so the lack of citations leaves all key premises unsupported.
premises: Compositional complexity, lattice distortion, and SRO at interfaces create heterogeneous obstacles
These obstacles foster dislocation nucleation and pileup
Dislocation nucleation and pileup promote gradual strain accumulation (creep)
Enhancing interface coherence/ordering reduces dislocation nucleation sites
Reducing nucleation sites leads to a lower creep rate
